name: Hornafjarðarmanni
description: Hornafjarðarmanni is a regional Icelandic trick-taking game, a variant of the broader 'Manni' family. It is distinctively played in the Hornafjörður region of south-east Iceland. It is a three-player game using a full deck and features a unique 'Manni' (Man) - a set of face-down cards that players can exchange with their hands to optimize their play.

history.origins: Derived from the Danish game 'Manni' or similar Scandinavian trick-taking games. It has been preserved as a localized tournament tradition in Hofn and Hornafjörður.
timeline: 20th Century: Hornafjarðarmanni stabilizes as a distinct regional variant.
Present: Annual tournaments are held in the region; it remains a symbol of local identity.
history.cultural: Significantly more than just a game; it is a cultural staple of the south-east coast that bridges generations.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard Manni by using a full 52-card deck (most Manni variants use 48 or 40) and refining the contract selection rules.

setup.players: Three players only. The player to dealer's left may exchange up to 7 cards with the Manni, then the player to dealer's right up to 5, then the dealer with the remainder; left of dealer leads to the first trick.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 16 cards to each player (in batches of 4) and 4 cards face-down in the center to form the 'Manni'.

rules.objective: Score points by winning more than 4 tricks in a hand. Points are awarded for each trick over 4.
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: Player to dealer's left.
2. Must follow suit. If unable, can play any card (including trump).
3. Highest trump (or highest card of suit led) wins the trick.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Hornafjarðarmanni.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - 5 tricks: 1 point.
Winning condition: Score points by winning more than 4 tricks in a hand.

strategy.basic: Prioritize winning at least 5 tricks to avoid a zero-score hand. If your hand is weak, use the Manni to find a trump suit.
strategy.intermediate: Contract bidding is crucial. If you see your hand has many high cards across suits, a 'No-Trump' (Nullo) or 'Grand' contract is more effective than a specific trump suit.
strategy.advanced: Tracking the Manni: If you saw the cards in the Manni before they were swapped, you have critical information about what cards your opponents are now holding.
tips: The Ace and King of the trump suit are the most powerful cards for securing your base 5 tricks.
In tournaments, playing conservatively to simply 'be on the board' is often better than aggressive bidding.

scoring.description: Points awarded for winning tricks exceeding 4. Each additional trick above 4 equals one point.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 30-50 points (agreed beforehand) wins.
